title: A login endpoint
context: Users log in with email and password and get a token for the API. Assume `db`, `User` and `SECRET` exist.

findings.d: Fast and unsalted, so leaked hashes are cracked in bulk. Use a slow, salted hash (argon2 via pwdlib, or bcrypt) and its verify function.
`"user": user` serialises every column, password_hash included. Add a response model (UserOut) with only safe fields.

findings.t: Different errors reveal which emails exist
findings.d: 404 "no such user" vs 401 "wrong password" lets anyone enumerate accounts. Return the same 401 for both.
No `exp` claim: a leaked token works forever. Add `exp` and decode with explicit `algorithms=[...]`.
`random` is predictable. Use `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`.
Simple-typed params are query params, so the password lands in URLs and access logs. Take a Pydantic body (or OAuth2 form) instead. Also: no rate limit on login.

title: An async report
context: Fetches the status of each of a customer's devices from a vendor API and returns a summary.

findings.d: requests.get, time.sleep and the sync DB call all block the event loop: one slow report stalls every request on the worker. Use httpx.AsyncClient and asyncio.sleep (and an async DB), or make the handler plain `def`.

findings.t: No timeout on the vendor call
findings.d: requests has no default timeout; a hung vendor hangs the request (and with the bug above, the worker). Always pass a timeout.
Vendor errors, JSON errors and typos all vanish; the report silently omits devices. Catch httpx/requests errors, log them, and mark the device as unknown.
N devices × (latency + 0.1 s). With an async client, run them concurrently with asyncio.gather and a semaphore to stay polite.
Anyone can request any customer's report (IDOR). Depend on the current user and check ownership.
Server-local time with no zone. Use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.

title: Listing orders
context: Returns a user's orders with item counts, optionally sorted by a column the client chooses.

findings.d: `sort` is pasted into the SQL. Identifiers can't be bound parameters, so map it through an allow-list: `{"created_at": Order.created_at, ...}[sort]`, else 422.
`db = SessionLocal()` is shared by all requests and threads; one error poisons it for everyone. Use a per-request session via Depends(get_db) with yield.
Any caller can list any user's orders. Derive the user from auth, or check `user_id == current_user.id`.
One get() and one lazy load of items per row. Query Orders with `selectinload(Order.items)` (or a COUNT with GROUP BY).
Returns every order ever. Add limit/offset with a capped maximum.
`float(order.total)` introduces rounding errors. Keep Decimal and serialise as a string, or use integer cents.

title: Settings and a cache
context: A small helper module imported by several routers.

findings.t: Auth fails open when API_KEY is unset
findings.d: `if not API_KEY or ...` lets everyone in when the env var is missing. Fail closed: refuse to start (or deny) without a key; compare with hmac.compare_digest.
Shared between calls; and `extend` mutates the cached profile, so tags pile up across requests. Default to None and don't mutate shared objects.
Evaluated once, so seen_at never changes. Default to None and compute inside (aware UTC).
Grows forever, never invalidates, differs per worker, and hands one request's mutations to the next. Use a bounded TTL cache or none.
`os.environ.get("DEBUG", True)` is True when unset, and any set string (even "false") is truthy. Parse explicitly, default False (pydantic-settings does this).
Timing leak. Use hmac.compare_digest.

title: Transferring credit
context: Moves credit between two accounts the caller owns.

findings.d: If the second update fails, the debit is committed and the credit isn't. Do both in one transaction (`with db.begin():`).
Read-check-write in Python: two concurrent transfers both see enough balance. Lock rows (`with_for_update()`) or update atomically with a `balance >= amount` condition and check the row count.
`user` is never used: anyone can move anyone's money. Load accounts filtered by owner_id.
A negative amount moves money the other way. `amount: Decimal = Field(gt=0)` in TransferIn. Also from_id == to_id.
db.get returns None for unknown ids, then `.balance` raises AttributeError. Return 404.
Insufficient funds returns 200 with ok: false. Use 409 (or 422) via HTTPException.

title: A test file
context: Tests for a certificate-expiry endpoint that also calls a vendor revocation API.
code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app, get_db
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

client = TestClient(app)
app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: test_session

def test_expiring_soon():
    cert = make_cert(not_after=datetime.now() + timedelta(days=1))
    r = client.get(f"/certs/{cert.serial}")
    assert r.status_code == 200

def test_revoked():
    r = client.get("/certs/REVOKED-1")      # real vendor API
    time.sleep(2)                           # wait for vendor
    assert r.json()["revoked"] is True

findings.d: Flaky, slow and dependent on the network and vendor data. Override the HTTP client dependency with httpx.MockTransport.
`datetime.now()` (naive, local) plus a 1-day window breaks near midnight or across zones. Inject a fixed aware `now`.
test_expiring_soon never checks the expiry flag or days left: it passes even if the logic is wrong. Assert the body.

findings.t: Overrides set globally and never cleared
findings.d: Set at import and leaked into every other test file. Use a fixture that sets and clears `dependency_overrides`.
The request already completed; sleeping only slows the suite. With a fake transport there's nothing to wait for.
TestClient outside a `with` block doesn't run lifespan, so startup-created clients and engines don't exist. Use `with TestClient(app) as client` in a fixture.
